metric: market size of outsourced small molecule CDMO
notes: No utilization figure, shortage metric or booking lead time located for innovator small-molecule API despite targeted search; absence of a lead-time signal in a market this size is itself evidence of slack. Saturation multiple is the loosest estimate in the table.

metric: GMP warning letters citing 21 CFR 211, FY2025
notes: Highest GMP warning letter count in over 20 years; 59% to US facilities. Compliance capacity, not physical capacity, is the tightening variable for small molecule.

metric: installed bioreactor capacity, Samsung Biologics
notes: Company reports full utilization of Plants 1-3 through 2025 and Plant 4 reaching full utilization in Q3 2025. Utilization entered as 95 to represent company-stated 'full'.

metric: installed bioreactor capacity, Lonza Vacaville
notes: Lonza reports high contracting volumes and +32.2% CER sales growth in Integrated Biologics; no utilization percentage disclosed.

metric: supplier-declared IND support capacity, single CDMO
notes: WuXi Biologics states regulatory submission capacity for ~200 INDs and 20 BLAs/MAAs per year. Clinical tier has headroom; commercial tier does not. Utilization inferred from the stated proxy rule.

metric: kickoff to first released GMP batch
notes: 9-15 months typical, 12-18+ for commercial transfers; Lonza markets a 5-month fast-track best case. Trade-publication source, weak provenance.

metric: batch rejection rate before/after right-first-time programme
notes: GSK case: 5.2% falling to 0.8% in eight months. Establishes the achievable range for established biologics manufacturing; well below CGT failure rates.

metric: CDMO share of global biologics capacity, 2028 projection
notes: Up from 43% in 2024. Vendor model, methodology not public.

metric: outsourced bioconjugation market size
notes: TIGHTNESS CLAIM NOT VERIFIED BY A UTILIZATION OR BOOKING-LEAD-TIME MEASUREMENT. No CDMO publishes conjugation suite utilization or slot lead time; the 80% utilization and 6-month lead time are inferred under the stated proxy rule, not observed.

metric: Lonza Visp conjugation suites, current to planned
notes: +40% suites at one flagship site. Demand growth of 20-30%/yr consumes that expansion in roughly two years.

metric: ADC programmes at a single CDMO
notes: WuXi Biologics: 252 ADC and 196 bispecific programmes, each modality growing ~30% year on year; ADCs plus bispecifics were two-thirds of new project additions.

metric: Swissmedic-approved aseptic line covering mAb, bispecific and ADC
notes: Integration of conjugation with ADC-capable aseptic filling is the specific scarce asset; general fill-finish lines are not ADC-qualified (containment).

metric: wait for an allocated manufacturing slot
notes: Slots are rationed rather than queued. One batch equals one dose, so capacity scales strictly linearly with suites and trained operators - no batch-size lever exists.

metric: apheresis to infusion
notes: Reported range 3-6 weeks; 2-4 weeks of that is manufacture plus release testing. Next-generation processes claim final formulation within 24 h but are not the commercial standard.

metric: share of patients not receiving product
notes: Range 4-7% of patients; clinical trial reported range 1-13%.

metric: LBCL commercial CAR-T manufacturing failure
notes: 38 of 981 approved patients, UK National CAR T Panel. Registry-grade denominator, the strongest single figure in this row set.

metric: OOS rate, CD19-directed CAR-T
notes: Range 1-6%; 5% specifically for liso-cel. OOS product is often still infused under expanded access, so OOS is not equivalent to a lost patient.

metric: manufacturing COGS per patient dose
notes: 2019 estimate was USD 95,780; working range USD 100,000-300,000. Modelled, not audited plant cost; excludes R&D and capital recovery.

metric: patient doses per clean suite per year
notes: Derived: 365/21-day cycle x 0.94 manufacturing success. A 10-suite facility yields ~163 doses/year.

metric: manufacturing COGS per dose
notes: 2019 estimate USD 4,460; recent estimates near USD 40,000, with one platform claim of USD 10-20k at 20,000-60,000 doses/year. Wide dispersion; all modelled.

metric: cost ratio, autologous to allogeneic COGS per dose
notes: 115,000 / 40,000 = 2.9x on recent estimates, versus 21x on the 2019 estimates. Allogeneic escapes the one-batch-one-dose constraint that makes autologous inelastic.

metric: AAV suite utilization
notes: OVERBUILD CLAIM: the <50% utilization number traces only to secondary aggregators (Mordor, IntuitionLabs) with undisclosed methodology - circular_risk true. It is corroborated by hard corporate events, not by an independent utilization measurement.

metric: National Resilience sites closed in 2025
notes: Corroborating hard event for the overbuild claim: capacity is leaving the system, which is not consistent with a capacity crunch.

metric: sale price of an FDA-approved commercial viral vector plant
notes: 125,000 sq ft, FDA-approved for commercial-scale viral vector, two GMP drug substance suites plus fill-finish, sold to OXB. A distressed price is the most legible evidence of excess supply in the whole dataset.

metric: manufacturing slot lead time
notes: Coexists with idle suites. Read as a tier mismatch - commercial-grade, high-titre, low-empty-capsid suites are booked while early-phase suites are idle - not as aggregate scarcity.

metric: empty capsid fraction in standard production
notes: Range 70-90%; industry target below 30%, aspiration below 10%. Reducing empty content is projected to cut cost 30-60% by lowering required dose.

metric: labelled systemic dose, muscle-directed AAV
notes: Three acute liver failure deaths in 2025 across Elevidys and SRP-9004; FDA boxed warning and narrowed indication. Dose, not manufacturing slots, is the binding constraint for systemic muscle AAV.

metric: order to released GMP lentiviral batch
notes: Range 8-14 months. Utilization inferred from lead time under the stated proxy rule.

metric: vector cost per dose at 2,000 L
notes: At 50 L the same model gives ~17 doses at ~USD 19,127 per dose - a ~13x unit-cost penalty. Demand cannot be absorbed by running small campaigns.

metric: lentiviral vector share of cell therapy manufacturing cost
notes: Oxford Biomedica batches to Novartis reported at USD 1.5m each, under 300 patient doses per batch.

metric: industry average plasmid lead time
notes: Above 12 months to access GMP plasmid capacity per 2025 commentary; 3-5 months of actual GMP production. Source for the 10-month figure is a 2022 company press release with no cited origin - treat as dated and single-source.

metric: agarose chromatography resin capacity addition
notes: Purolite plant; downstream purification still described as the primary bottleneck after it came online. Moderna's new UK/AU/CA plants alone absorb hundreds of GMP plasmid batches annually.

metric: line utilization versus nameplate
notes: Sources state advanced mRNA lines run at 'a fraction of nameplate'; no numeric utilization is published. The 16% is an assumption entered to make the derivation explicit, not an observation.

metric: immediate settlement payment, Arbutus/Genevant v Moderna
notes: Plus a further USD 1.3bn provided for. The binding mRNA-LNP constraint is the cost of freedom to operate on the ionizable lipid, not reactor time.

metric: Alnylam cationic lipid suits resolved on non-infringement
notes: Federal Circuit for Moderna 4 Jun 2025, settled 15 Sep 2025 with no payment; Pfizer non-infringement judgment 30 Jul 2025. The claim-construction of 'cationic lipid' is outcome-determinative, so FTO risk is narrower than the Arbutus outcome alone suggests.

metric: VX-522 inhaled CFTR mRNA-LNP terminated
notes: Persistent lung inflammation attributed to the LNP; efficacy never assessed. Tolerability, not manufacturability, ended the programme.

metric: cGMP synthesis capacity at the largest single site
notes: Nitto Avecia Milford, described at the time as the largest oligonucleotide site in the world. Figure is dated; used as a scale anchor, not a current-capacity estimate.

metric: Agilent nucleic-acid manufacturing expansion
notes: Customer shipments from the expansion begin 2026. Clinical-tier oligo demand is grams to low kilograms and is not utilization-limited; the constrained tier is commercial multi-hundred-kilogram siRNA supply.

metric: vaccine contract manufacturing market size
notes: Rising to USD 4.33bn in 2026. No installed dose capacity or utilization figure with a public methodology was located; global vaccine capacity is documented as poorly defined and inconsistently measured.

metric: CDMO consolidation tightening sterile fill-finish availability
notes: Late-stage vaccine sponsors reported facing sterile line capacity constraints. Adjective-level claim; no utilization number published.

metric: time to build and qualify a new aseptic line
notes: 2-3 years typical, over 5 for complex formats. Utilization of 85 is an assumption under the stated proxy rule, not an observation - no fill-finish utilization percentage is published anywhere located.

metric: disclosed CDMO capital investment announcements
notes: About three-quarters flowed to US facilities, reflecting reshoring policy. Capital is not the constraint; the 3-year construction lag and format non-fungibility are.

metric: published CRLs citing quality or manufacturing issues
notes: 150 of 202 CRLs published July 2025 for applications issued 2020-2024. Decisive caveat: every application in that cohort was later approved, so the figure measures delay, not prevention.

metric: facility plus quality/CMC share of all CRL deficiency citations
notes: Exceeds clinical safety (13.4%) and efficacy (10.9%) combined.

metric: CRLs released for pending or withdrawn applications
notes: Second batch, September 2025. This is the correct denominator for 'how often does manufacturing stop an approval', and no source located has decomposed it by deficiency type.

metric: share of marketing application non-approvals attributable to CMC
notes: CMC is also the second most common reason for oncology IND clinical holds after clinical considerations. Denominator undisclosed - single secondary source.

metric: FDA platform technology designations granted
notes: First to Sarepta (AAVrh74) June 2025, revoked about a month later after three deaths; second to Krystal Biotech (HSV-1) October 2025. Practical throughput effect to date is approximately zero.

metric: FDA states no requirement to manufacture three PPQ lots
notes: January 2026 announcement also covers lighter comparability for minor development changes and revisable BLA release specifications. Covington notes it does not change underlying legal requirements.

metric: risk-based comparability framework for CGT manufacturing changes
notes: Every manufacturing change requires a risk assessment; for CGT the process defines the product, so comparability is materially harder than for mAbs and is the main reason CGT process improvements are not adopted mid-development.

metric: commercial IND submissions received by CDER
notes: Plus 716 research INDs, total 1,855 receipts. Excludes biosimilar, expanded access and unknown INDs.

metric: active cell and gene therapy INDs at CBER OTP
notes: About 1,300 of them gene therapy INDs. This is a stock, not an annual flow; dividing by a ~7-year active life implies roughly 350 new CGT INDs per year.

metric: IND-volume multiple at which the first sub-capacity saturates
notes: GMP plasmid DNA and lentiviral vector bind first, then aseptic fill-finish (1.12x), then autologous CAR-T slots and ADC conjugation (1.19x), then AAV suites (1.5-1.9x). Spread to the loosest (small molecule, 10x) is 9.4x.

metric: approvals response to a 10% manufacturing improvement
notes: System-wide elasticity ~0.05, an order of magnitude below what a true system constraint would show. Within autologous CAR-T, elasticity on patients treated approaches 1.0.

metric: tumour-to-liver delivery ratio in humans
notes: 0.01 %ID/g human tumour against a conservative 40 %ID to liver. Roughly 4,000-fold. This ratio is the quantitative statement of why hepatic indications reached market first.

metric: human solid tumour antibody uptake
notes: Versus ~30 %ID/g in mouse xenografts, a ~3,000-fold difference driven principally by body-mass scaling. Unchanged over the decade - improvement rate on the transport metric is 0-fold.

metric: brain uptake with TfR1 shuttle, mouse
notes: About 80-fold over the unmodified parent antibody, implying an unshuttled baseline near 0.03 %ID/g.

metric: brain exposure increase with TfR1 shuttle, primate
notes: Attenuated roughly 5-20x relative to the mouse figure but clinically confirmed: 91% of participants below 24 centiloids at 28 weeks at 3.6 mg/kg with ARIA-E under 5%.

metric: first approval of a receptor-mediated-transcytosis brain delivery platform product
notes: Tividenofusp alfa (AVLAYAH), accelerated approval 25 March 2026 for neurologic manifestations of Hunter syndrome.

metric: incremental amyloid SUVR reduction from focused ultrasound BBB opening
notes: In FUS-treated regions versus antibody alone over 26 weeks; preclinical work showed a 5-6 fold antibody concentration increase. Adjunctive and device-bound; does not scale to chronic systemic dosing.

metric: transfer of murine capsid gain to primates, non-conserved-receptor selections
notes: PHP.B/PHP.eB depend on murine-restricted LY6A and fail in BALB/c, NHP and human; MyoAAV diminished in NHP; LK03 shows the mirror-image failure. The fix - selecting on conserved receptors CA-IV and ALPL - is a methodology change, not a physical barrier.

metric: target knockdown in NHP adipose tissue
notes: Plus up to 80% kidney proximal tubule knockdown from rodent through NHP. Company press release, assay undisclosed - low provenance, no clinical confirmation.

metric: first-in-human dosing of CD8-targeted LNP delivering CAR mRNA
notes: Capstan CPTX2309; NHP two-dose cycle produced deep B-cell depletion with naive B-cell repopulation. If it holds, it removes the autologous manufacturing constraint entirely rather than relieving it.

metric: extrahepatic receptor-ligand systems matching GalNAc-ASGPR efficiency and recyclability
notes: Reviews state none exists; critically low endosomal escape and tissue-specific barriers remain limiting.
